chapter: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
title: The Paradise Club and the Clarence Profit Trio
summary: He tells of the Paradise on Main Street, where Goodman found Hampton, and says he told Nat Cole not to join Hampton's band after hearing the Clarence Profit Trio.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But that's a club that you might not have heard of.

The Paradise Club used to have bands, and the former boxer, a middleweight boxer called Papke, Billy Papke -- he used to have a nightclub. There were just so many clubs that they had, you know, around, and it's amazing that, as you say, that people didn't realize how much music was going on in Los Angeles.

So anyway, oh yeah -- I was gonna tell you about Lionel. Well, Lionel wanted the trio -- wanted Nat's trio and me; that was gonna be the nucleus, you know. And Nat and them were so close that they really wanted to go, but on my trip to New York that year ... I met and heard the trio that was the talk of New York; it was called the Clarence Profit Trio. Did you know of Clarence Profit Trio? There was a Clarence Profit Trio in New York, and all New York was raving about them, and I sat up and listened to them night after night, and I came back and I told Nat and Oscar and them and I asked him, I said, "Hey, don't join the band. You got to stay by yourself, because you'll just kill everybody if you go to New York, because you know, what they were playing and what you're playing, they haven't heard that in New York; they haven't heard that anyplace, and you really got to stay together", because you know, they were so smooth, and the piano and guitar things were really intelligent things they were playing, you know, and they were really difficult to play.
